style.vernacular: Low coral-atoll town on a strip under 3 m above sea level: one- and two-storey concrete-block buildings, rendered or whitewashed in pale blue, green and cream, under corrugated galvanised or rust-red iron roofs; multi-storey buildings are very uncommon. Traditional open-sided maneaba meeting houses with huge steep pandanus-thatch or iron roofs and low eaves; thatch houses on posts; coconut palms, pandanus, ironwood and mangroves on coral sand.
style.ornament: Maneaba: very large steep roof reaching almost to the ground on coconut-timber posts with coral-stone bases, lashed with coconut-fibre sinnet, open sides; modern buildings are plain with louvre windows, deep eaves and painted concrete plinths; blank painted boards for signage.

sources.what: multi-storey buildings very uncommon; dense low-rise houses; causeways link islets; coconut palms, mangroves and ironwood; land mostly under 3 m
maneaba roof of coconut timber on coral supports, pandanus-leaf thatch, tied with coconut string
Bairiki islet under half a km2 at 3 m elevation, government ministries and State House, National Stadium
